sights.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
sights.area: Cu Chi (outer Ho Chi Minh City)
sights.addr: Bến Đình (xã Nhuận Đức) hoặc Bến Dược (xã An Nhơn Tây), Củ Chi cũ, TP.HCM
sights.short: Yes, if you want to understand the war from the Vietnamese side. The tunnels are about 70 km from the city centre, so the real question is how you get there: a half-day tour is easiest, the public bus is cheap but slow. There are two sites, Ben Dinh (closer, busier) and Ben Duoc (further, quieter).
why: A network of about 250 km of tunnels dug from 1948 and joined into one system in the 1960s, with kitchens, meeting rooms and field hospitals underground.
You can crawl through a short, widened section, see hidden trapdoors and booby traps, and taste steamed cassava, the wartime staple.
It is one of Vietnam's most visited sites and ranks among Tripadvisor's top attractions in Asia (CafeF, June 2026).
sights.status: Open daily from 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, holidays included. Published 2026 prices differ between sources (85,000 or 125,000 dong for foreign adults; 35,000 dong for Vietnamese adults; children 7–16 half price, under 7 free), so trust the board at the gate. Most tours include the ticket.
facts: About 125,000 dong for foreign adults; check the board at the gate
Half a day including travel; 1.5–2 hours on site
Ben Dinh: closer and set up for tours. Ben Duoc: further, quieter, with a memorial temple
getting: Half-day tour from District 1 (by bus, or by speedboat on the Saigon River): the easiest option, ticket and guide usually included.
Public bus to Ben Duoc: bus 13 from Saigon bus station to Cu Chi bus station, then bus 79. Allow 2+ hours each way; city buses are free until 31 Dec 2026.
From Cholon: bus 94 from Cholon bus station to Cu Chi, then bus 79.
Ride-hailing car: about 1.5–2 hours each way depending on traffic; agree on a wait-and-return if you book by the hour.
tips: Start early: mornings are cooler and the busiest tour groups arrive late morning.
Wear clothes you don't mind getting dusty, closed shoes and insect repellent.
The tunnels are tight and dark: skip the crawl if you are claustrophobic; there is plenty to see above ground.
A shooting range on site sells bullets for real wartime rifles; it is loud and optional.

tour.h: Book a Cu Chi Tunnels tour
tour.p: Half-day tours pick you up in District 1 and usually include the entrance ticket and an English-speaking guide, which saves the 2+ hour bus ride each way.
tour.label: See Cu Chi Tunnels tours on Klook ↗
extra: Cu Chi + Mekong Delta in one day? See Mekong Delta day tours ↗

sights.teaser: How to get there, which site to pick, and whether to book a tour.

sights.name: War Remnants Museum
sights.vn: Bảo tàng Chứng tích Chiến tranh
sights.addr: 28 Võ Văn Tần, phường Xuân Hòa (Quận 3 cũ), TP.HCM
sights.short: Yes, it is the city's most visited museum and the clearest introduction to the war's human cost. Some galleries, especially on Agent Orange, are very graphic: plan two hours and some quiet time afterwards. Tickets are cheap and can now be bought online to skip the queue.
why: Photo galleries by war photographers from many countries, including those who died covering the conflict.
Tanks, aircraft and artillery in the courtyard, and a reconstruction of the 'tiger cage' prison cells.
A 10-minute walk from the Independence Palace, so the two fit into one morning.
sights.status: Since 10 February 2026 tickets can be bought online at ticket.baotangchungtichchientranh.vn: choose a time slot, pay, and scan the emailed QR code at the entrance (SGGP).
facts: 7:30 am – 5:30 pm daily; ticket counter closes 5:00 pm
40,000 dong; students half price; under-6s free
getting: Walk: about 15 minutes from Ben Thanh Market, 10 minutes from the Independence Palace.
Metro Line 1: Ben Thanh station, then walk about 15 minutes.
Ride-hailing: ask for “Bảo tàng Chứng tích Chiến tranh”.
tips: Go at opening time: tour groups fill the galleries from mid-morning.
Start on the top floor and work down; the hardest galleries are on the upper floors and you can skip them.
It may not suit young children; parents often see the courtyard and ground floor only.
sights.teaser: Tickets, hours, online booking and how to handle the hardest galleries.

sights.name: Independence Palace
sights.addr: 135 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, phường Bến Thành (Quận 1 cũ), TP.HCM
sights.short: Yes: it is where the war ended on 30 April 1975, when a tank broke through the gate, and the 1960s building is almost untouched inside. Allow 1–1.5 hours, go down to the basement command bunker, and pair it with the War Remnants Museum nearby.
why: A rare, well-kept piece of 1960s modernist architecture, with the original meeting rooms, banquet hall and furniture.
The basement still holds the war-room maps, radio equipment and tunnels of the presidential bunker.
Replicas of the tanks that entered on 30 April 1975 stand in the grounds.
sights.status: Two ticket types: the palace alone, or a combo that adds the exhibition on the earlier Norodom Palace (1868–1966). Ticket sales stop at 3:30 pm (Vietnambooking, March 2026). The palace can close at short notice for state events.
facts: Main building 8:00 am – 4:30 pm; exhibition 8:30 am – 4:30 pm; tickets until 3:30 pm
40,000 dong (palace); 65,000 dong with the exhibition. Students 20,000 / 45,000
getting: Walk: about 10 minutes from Ben Thanh Market or Notre-Dame Cathedral.
Metro Line 1: Ben Thanh station, then about 10 minutes on foot.
Ride-hailing: ask for “Dinh Độc Lập”; the visitor entrance is on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia street.
tips: Arrive before 3:00 pm; the last ticket is sold at 3:30 pm.
Don't skip the basement: the bunker is the most atmospheric part.
Signs inside are short; a guided city tour or reading up beforehand adds a lot of context.
sights.teaser: Where the war ended: tickets, hours and the bunker not to miss.

sights.name: Mekong Delta day trip
sights.vn: Du lịch miền Tây: Mỹ Tho – Bến Tre
sights.area: My Tho and Ben Tre (Mekong Delta)
sights.addr: Bến tàu Mỹ Tho và các cồn Thới Sơn, Cồn Phụng trên sông Tiền
sights.short: Yes, if you want a taste of river life without staying overnight. A day trip to My Tho and Ben Tre means about two hours on the road each way, then boats between coconut-palm islands, fruit, honey tea and folk music. It is touristy but pleasant; for real floating markets you need to stay a night near Can Tho.
why: A boat ride on the wide Tien River past the 'four sacred animal' islands and the Rach Mieu bridge.
Paddling a small sampan through narrow coconut-palm canals, the photo everyone comes for.
Coconut candy workshops, honey tea, tropical fruit and đờn ca tài tử, the traditional music of the south.
sights.status: Most day tours leave District 1 around 7:00 am and are back in the late afternoon. A typical route: boat from My Tho pier, coconut candy workshop, Thoi Son island with honey tea and a horse cart, sampan ride with fruit and music, lunch on Con Phung, and Vinh Trang Pagoda on the way back (iVIVU tour sheet).
facts: A full day, roughly 7:00 am – 5:00 pm
About 2 hours each way by road
A first look at the delta without staying overnight
Not on most day trips; Cai Rang (Can Tho) needs an overnight stay
getting: Day tour with hotel or District 1 pickup: by far the easiest, with boats, lunch and guide included.
Combined Cu Chi Tunnels + Mekong day tours exist but are rushed; pick one if you can.
Going alone: intercity buses leave from the Mien Tay bus station; you then arrange boats at My Tho pier yourself.
tips: Bring sunscreen, a hat and insect repellent; boats have little shade.
Carry small notes for tips to the sampan rowers and musicians.
Small-group tours visit the same islands but feel much less crowded.

tour.h: Book a Mekong Delta day tour
tour.p: Day tours pick you up in District 1 and include the boats, lunch and a guide, so you spend the day on the river instead of arranging transport.
tour.label: See Mekong Delta day tours on Klook ↗

sights.teaser: Is a one-day Mekong trip worth it, what you'll do, and how to book.

sights.name: Landmark 81 SkyView
sights.addr: Landmark 81, Vinhomes Central Park, Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh, phường Thạnh Mỹ Tây (Bình Thạnh cũ)
sights.short: Yes, for the highest view in the city: the observation deck is on floors 79–81 of Vietnam's tallest building. Go late afternoon to see sunset and the lights come on, and come by metro to Tan Cang station. Tickets are pricier at weekends, so a weekday visit saves money.
why: 360° views over the Saigon River, District 1's skyline and the new Thu Thiem area.
A glass floor, telescopes and the 'Skytouch' open-air challenge on the top floor, with safety gear.
Bars and restaurants on floor 79 if you want to stay for a drink after dark.
sights.status: Reference prices (MIA.vn, Dec 2025) for the combo with a VR experience and a printed photo: about 420,000 dong for adults on weekdays and 500,000 dong at weekends; children about 220,000 / 250,000 dong. Buy online at least 2 hours ahead or at the counter on basement B1.
facts: About 420,000 dong weekdays, 500,000 dong weekends (adult combo)
4:00 pm onwards for sunset and night views
getting: Metro Line 1: Tan Cang station, then a short walk to Vinhomes Central Park.
Ride-hailing: ask for “Landmark 81”, about 20–25 minutes from Ben Thanh depending on traffic.
Ticket counter: basement B1 of Vincom Landmark 81.
tips: Check the weather: on hazy or rainy days the view drops a lot.
Drinking water and dangerous items are not allowed in; finish your drink before security.
Weekday tickets are cheaper and the deck is quieter.

tour.p: Booking online lets you pick your time slot and walk straight up, which helps at sunset when the counter gets busy.
tour.label: See Landmark 81 SkyView tickets on Klook ↗

sights.teaser: The city's highest view: tickets, best time and getting there by metro.

sights.name: Saigon River dinner cruise
sights.vn: Du thuyền ăn tối trên sông Sài Gòn
sights.addr: Các bến du thuyền dọc sông Sài Gòn (Quận 1, Quận 4 cũ)
sights.short: Worth it if you want an easy, relaxed evening: two hours on the river with dinner and the lit-up skyline. The food is buffet or set menus rather than the city's best, so treat it as a view with dinner. Book ahead for weekends and holidays.
why: The best way to see the skyline at night, including Landmark 81 and the Thu Thiem bridges.
Buffet or set-menu dinner on board, often with live music.
A calm break from motorbike traffic, good for families and couples.
sights.status: Dinner cruises usually board around 6:30–7:00 pm and return around 9:00–9:30 pm. Buffet cruises start at about 500,000 dong per person, with higher decks and fine-dining boats costing more; drinks and VAT are often extra (Vietnambooking, MIA.vn).
facts: Board around 6:30–7:00 pm, back around 9:00–9:30 pm
From about 500,000 dong per person (buffet); more for upper decks and fine dining
getting: Piers are in District 1 (around Bach Dang) and District 4 (near Nha Rong wharf); your ticket names the exact pier.
Ride-hailing is easiest; arrive 30 minutes before departure.
On a budget, the river bus from Bach Dang pier gives similar views for a fraction of the price (no dinner).
tips: Check exactly what is included: drinks, VAT and transfers vary a lot between boats.
Ask for an upper or outdoor deck for the best views.
Bring a light layer: it can be windy on deck.

tour.p: Compare boats, decks and what is included, and lock in a table for the night you want.
tour.label: See Saigon River dinner cruises on Klook ↗

sights.teaser: Two hours on the river with dinner: what to expect, prices and piers.

sights.name: Saigon Notre-Dame Cathedral
sights.vn: Nhà thờ Chính tòa Đức Bà Sài Gòn
sights.addr: 01 Công xã Paris, phường Sài Gòn (Quận 1 cũ)
sights.short: Yes, go, but mostly for the outside for now. The red-brick cathedral has been under a major restoration since 2017 and is wrapped in scaffolding; inside access has been limited to Mass and registered groups. It sits right next to the Central Post Office, so see both in one stop.
why: Built from 1877 to 1880 with materials shipped from Europe, it is Saigon's best-known colonial landmark and still a working cathedral.
In March 2026 two gilded crosses, each about 3.7 m tall and 400 kg, were lifted to the top of the bell tower, one of the restoration's big milestones.
The square in front, with the statue of the Virgin Mary, is a classic photo spot and a short walk from Nguyen Hue and Ben Thanh Market.
sights.status: Restoration began in July 2017, led by Belgium's Monument group. The original 2027 target will not be met because many parts are badly damaged; no new completion date has been given (Dân Trí, March 2026). In December 2025, the inside was open for Mass at 5:30 am and 5:30 pm and for registered pilgrim groups, but not yet for general sightseeing (Thanh Niên). Check at the gate when you visit.
facts: Mass (5:30 am and 5:30 pm daily, as of Dec 2025) and registered groups; general visits not yet reopened
20–30 minutes, more with the Post Office
getting: Metro Line 1: Opera House station, about a 10-minute walk.
City buses are free until 31 Dec 2026; many routes stop around Ben Thanh, about 15 minutes on foot.
Ride-hailing: ask for “Nhà thờ Đức Bà”.
tips: Come early morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer tour groups.
If you go in for Mass, cover shoulders and knees and stay quiet; photos during services are not appropriate.
The square is ringed by busy traffic: cross with the steady, slow walk locals use.
sights.teaser: Saigon's red-brick cathedral, mid-restoration: what you can see now.

sights.name: Saigon Central Post Office
sights.vn: Bưu điện Trung tâm Sài Gòn
sights.addr: 2 Công xã Paris, phường Sài Gòn (Quận 1 cũ)
sights.short: Yes. It is free, open every day from about 7 am to 7 pm, and right next to the Notre-Dame Cathedral. Step inside for the vaulted hall, old maps and wooden phone booths, and send a postcard from a post office that still works.
why: Built between 1886 and 1891, it is usually credited to the architect Alfred Foulhoux. The popular story that Gustave Eiffel designed it has no documentary evidence.
The main hall has a steel-ribbed glass vault, a clock over the entrance and two hand-drawn 19th-century maps on the walls.
Rows of wooden public telephone booths still line the hall, and you can buy stamps and post cards home.
facts: About 7:00 am – 7:00 pm daily, including most holidays (checked January 2026)
getting: Next door to the Notre-Dame Cathedral.
Metro Line 1: Opera House station, about a 10-minute walk.
Ride-hailing: ask for “Bưu điện Thành phố”.
tips: Mornings are calmer before tour buses arrive.
Souvenir stalls inside are convenient but not the cheapest; compare before buying.
Hours can shift slightly around Tết and national holidays.
sights.teaser: Free, open daily: a working 1890s post office with a glass-vaulted hall.

sights.name: Nguyen Hue Walking Street and the Opera House
sights.vn: Phố đi bộ Nguyễn Huệ · Nhà hát Thành phố
sights.addr: Đường Nguyễn Huệ, phường Sài Gòn (Quận 1 cũ)
sights.short: Yes, go in the evening. The pedestrian boulevard runs about 670 m from the City Hall area down towards the Saigon River, is free and open around the clock, and is at its liveliest after dark, especially at weekends. The Opera House is a few minutes' walk away on Le Loi.
why: The central section became a pedestrian square around 2015 and is now Saigon's main open-air living room: families, skaters, buskers and dancers by the fountain in the evening.
A large bronze statue of Ho Chi Minh stands at the top end in front of the colonial City Hall; the other end opens towards the river.
Early mornings are for locals: tai chi, badminton and runners from about 6:30 to 8:00 am.
Around Lunar New Year the street turns into the Tết flower street, one of the city's biggest seasonal displays.
getting: Metro Line 1: Opera House station, a few minutes' walk.
From Ben Thanh Market, walk east along Le Loi for about 10 minutes.
Walk to the river end for Bach Dang pier, where the river bus leaves.
tips: Come after sunset when it is cooler and the buildings are lit.
Keep your phone away from the kerb side: snatching from passing motorbikes happens in busy areas.
Many cafés sit in the old apartment blocks along the street; look for the stairwells with café signs.
sights.teaser: The city's open-air living room, best after dark, by the Opera House.

sights.name: Ben Thanh Market
sights.addr: Chợ Bến Thành, phường Bến Thành (Quận 1 cũ)
sights.short: Worth a look for the building and the food stalls, but it is the city's most touristy market: prices for souvenirs start high. The market runs from about 6 am to 6 pm, then a night market sets up on the side streets until about 10 pm. Metro Line 1 starts right next to it.
why: The current building with its famous clock tower was finished in 1914 and is one of Saigon's symbols.
Inside you will find clothes, coffee, dried fruit and a food section where you can try many Vietnamese dishes under one roof.
After 6 pm, stalls on Phan Bội Châu and Phan Chu Trinh streets add an evening market with more food.
facts: About 6:00 am – 6:00 pm; night market on the side streets until about 10:00 pm
getting: Metro Line 1: Ben Thanh station is right next to the market.
Airport bus 152 runs via Ben Thanh Market; city buses are free until 31 Dec 2026.
Ride-hailing: ask for “Chợ Bến Thành”.
tips: Ask the price before you order or buy, and bargain politely for souvenirs.
Crowds attract pickpockets: carry your bag in front.
For more local markets, head to Cholon: Binh Tay, Phung Hung and Hoa Binh.
sights.teaser: The 1914 clock-tower market: food stalls by day, night market after 6 pm.

sights.name: Thien Hau Temple (Tue Thanh Assembly Hall)
sights.vn: Chùa Bà Thiên Hậu · Hội quán Tuệ Thành
sights.addr: 710 Nguyễn Trãi, phường Chợ Lớn (Quận 5 cũ)
sights.short: Yes, it is one of the most atmospheric temples in Cholon. The Cantonese community's assembly hall honours Thiên Hậu, goddess of the sea, and is known for its ceramic roof figures and giant hanging incense coils. Open daily about 6:30 am to 4:30 pm.
why: Founded by Chinese families from Guangzhou (Tuệ Thành), it was already recorded around 1820; inscriptions on its bell and incense burner date to 1830.
The roof, walls and eaves are lined with ceramic figures telling Chinese stories, and the central courtyard light well lets sun fall through the incense smoke.
People hang spiral incense coils that burn for days as prayers; the temple keeps hundreds of antique pieces.
facts: Vía Bà, 22nd–24th day of the 3rd lunar month (very crowded)
getting: Ride-hailing from District 1 takes about 20–30 minutes depending on traffic.
City bus 1 runs from the centre to Cholon (free until 31 Dec 2026).
Combine with Lantern Street, the herbal medicine street and Phung Hung Market nearby.
tips: Dress modestly, speak softly and ask before photographing people praying.
Do not touch altars or offerings; donations are welcome.
Mornings are quieter and the light through the courtyard is best.
sights.teaser: Cholon's Cantonese temple of the sea goddess, with giant incense coils.

sights.name: Binh Tay Market
sights.addr: 57A Tháp Mười, phường Bình Tây (Quận 6 cũ)
sights.short: Yes, it is Cholon's grand old market and far more local than Ben Thanh. Come in the morning for the wholesale bustle and breakfast stalls, or in the evening for the Cholon night street of food stalls around the market (daily 6 pm to midnight).
why: Built in 1928 and opened in 1930, it was funded by the merchant Quách Đàm, whose statue stands in the courtyard. Its Chinese-style roofs make it one of Saigon's most photogenic buildings.
It is a working wholesale market: dried goods, spices, kitchenware and snacks sold by the sack.
Since December 2025 the Phố đêm Chợ Lớn night street fills the four streets around the market with food stalls and food trucks every evening.
facts: Daily 6:00 pm – midnight around the market
getting: City bus 1 ends at Cholon bus station near the market (free until 31 Dec 2026).
Ride-hailing from District 1 takes about 25–35 minutes depending on traffic.
Ask for “Chợ Bình Tây”.
tips: Inside the market, try bún thịt nướng and chè nhãn nhục (longan sweet soup), as recommended in creators' videos.
Wholesale stalls may not sell single items; snack and souvenir stalls do.
Keep bags zipped in the crowded aisles.
sights.teaser: Cholon's grand 1930 market, plus a nightly street-food market around it.
